senses.definition: (computing, programming) A data structure, especially one that serves to group a number of fields (in contrast to an object-oriented class with methods) or one that is passed by value rather than by reference.

quotes.text: Note that because structs are value types, the new operator does not work in the same way as it does for classes and other reference types.
quotes.reference: 2005, Christian Nagel, Bill Evjen, Jay Glynn, Karli Watson, Morgan Skinner, Allen Jones, Professional C# 2005, John Wiley & Sons, →ISBN, page 103:

quotes.text: Like most object-oriented languages, including Objective-C, Swift supports two basic object-oriented data structures: classes and structs.
